label: Another big day

what_happens.title: What happens on the big day
goals: The big day has steps in order, and each step is short
The child knows where they go and what comes after
The day has an end, and then home
what_happens.parentSkill: Tell the steps of the day in order and ask your child what comes next.

who_is_there.title: Who will be there
goals: New people have jobs, and they are there to help
The grown-up stays close or comes back at a set time
Other children may be there too
who_is_there.parentSkill: Name each new person by their job, and say where you will be.

what_i_do.title: What I can do
goals: The child's own small jobs on the day
Asking for help or a break with simple words
Something to hold or look forward to
what_i_do.parentSkill: Give your child one small job and one sentence to ask for help.

if_scared.title: If I feel scared
goals: Feeling scared or unsure is okay
Calm tools: slow breaths, a hand to hold, counting
The grown-up is there or comes back
if_scared.parentSkill: Name the feeling and stay calm: 'You feel nervous. That's okay. I'm here.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the big day
goals: Act out the day with toys
Practise the help sentence and the calm tools
Go through the steps once more, ending at home
rehearsal.parentSkill: Play the day with toys and let your child lead.

steps: Travel to the place with a grown-up
Say hello to the people there
Do the main part of the day, one step at a time
Go home and talk about it
Celebrate being brave with a hug
sensory: a new room with new smells
bright lights or a busy place
a place that feels big and new
waiting in a line or a waiting room
honestyNotes: The parent's label describes the event; do not invent details about it. Never promise how it will feel or that nothing will go wrong. Promise only what is true: the grown-up is there or comes back.

fallbackAnswer: First we go there together, then we do it one step at a time.
[[GROWNUP]] will be there with you, or will come back at the time you agree.
You can ask [[GROWNUP]] where they will be.
You can hold a hand, take slow breaths, and ask for help.
There may be new people whose job is to help.
You can say hello, or just wave.
[[GROWNUP]] will tell you exactly what it may feel like.
[[GROWNUP]] will tell you how long it lasts, maybe as long as one cartoon.
Then it is over, and we go home.

questionButtons.text: What if I don't know what to do?
fallbackAnswer: You can watch first, or ask a grown-up there.
Nobody knows everything the first time.
After the big day, we go home and talk about it.
Maybe we will do something cosy together.

techniques.label: Holding hands
techniques.how: Offer your hand at the hard moments, or agree on a squeeze that means 'I'm here'.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Counting to ten
techniques.how: Count slowly to ten together during a hard part.

techniques.label: Steps in pictures
techniques.how: Draw the steps of the day and tick them off together.

techniques.label: Bringing a comfort toy
techniques.how: Bring a small favourite toy to hold.

techniques.label: A help sentence
techniques.how: Practise one sentence: 'Can you help me, please?' or 'I need a break.'

techniques.label: Watching first
techniques.how: Let your child watch the new thing from the side before joining in.

techniques.label: A quiet break
techniques.how: Agree a signal for a short break somewhere quiet, and take it when asked.

ritual: Get ready and say the plan
Do it one step at a time
Go home and share the best part

unknown: First we go there, then one step at a time, then home.
separation: I'll be right there, or I'll come back when we said.
Squeeze my hand if you need me.
safety: Feeling scared is okay. We'll do it together.
The people there know how to help.
strangers: Those people are there to help. Let's say hello.
You can stay close to me while you say hello.
pain: I'll tell you honestly how it might feel.
If something hurts, tell me and we'll stop and think.
sensory: It might be loud or bright. We can take a break.
Let's notice three things we can see.
body: Your body is yours. You can say 'stop' or 'I need a break'.
Tell me if anything feels wrong.
social: There may be other kids. You can say hi, or just watch first.
It's okay to take your time.
love: I love you, and I'm proud of you for trying.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] has a big day.
A big day is a new thing, and new things can feel big.
First, [[CHILD]] gets ready at home and hears the plan.
Then [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] go there together.
Each part of the day comes one step at a time.
Then [[CHILD]] arrives and looks around.
There may be new rooms, new sounds and new faces.
Next comes the main part of the day, one small step and then another.
After that, the big day is done.
[[CHILD]] goes home and tells the best part.
On the big day there may be new people.
Each new person has a job, and their job is to help.
[[CHILD]] can say hello, or just wave.
Some people talk a lot, and some are quiet.
It's fine to watch for a little while first.
[[GROWNUP]] is right there with [[CHILD]], or comes back at the time they agreed.
There may be other kids, too.
Some might be new, just like [[CHILD]].
[[CHILD]] can stay close to [[GROWNUP]] until it feels okay.
On the big day, [[CHILD]] has a few small jobs.
Listen to the helpers, one step at a time.
If [[CHILD]] needs help, [[CHILD]] can say, can you help me, please?
If [[CHILD]] needs a break, [[CHILD]] can say, I need a break.
Those are strong words.
[[CHILD]] can bring something to hold, like a small toy.
And there is a hand to hold, too.
[[GROWNUP]] and [[CHILD]] can make a special squeeze: three squeezes mean I'm here.
After the big day, there is something nice to look forward to at home.
Sometimes new things feel scary.
That is okay, and lots of children feel that way.
Feelings can be big, and then they get smaller.
[[CHILD]] can smell a flower and blow out a candle, slow and soft.
Then [[CHILD]] can ask a grown-up for help.
If it is too loud or too bright, [[CHILD]] can take a little break.
[[CHILD]] can count to ten or hold [[GROWNUP]]'s hand.
Brave does not mean not scared.
Brave means trying, with someone close by.
Tonight [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] act out the big day with toys.
First, the toys get ready and go there together.
Then a toy says hello to a new helper.
Next, the toy asks, can you help me, please?
Now try the slow flower breath together.
Let's say the big day once more.
First, get ready at home.
Then go there together, and do it one step at a time.
After that, go home and tell the best part.
[[GROWNUP]] is proud of [[CHILD]] for practising.
My name is [[CHILD]], and soon I have a big day.
A big day is something new.
First, I get ready at home.
Then I go there with [[GROWNUP]].
I can ask [[GROWNUP]] about the plan.
The day has parts that happen in order.
Next, we arrive at the place.
There may be new rooms and new sounds.
Then the main part of the day happens, one step at a time.
After that, the big day is done.
Then I go home.
I can tell [[GROWNUP]] about my day.
On the big day there may be new people.
New people there have jobs, and their jobs are to help.
I can say hello or wave.
Some people may talk to me.
I can watch first if I want to.
[[GROWNUP]] will be with me, or will come back at a time we know.
There may be other kids there too.
Some kids may be new, like me.
I can stay close to [[GROWNUP]] at first.
That is okay.
On the big day I listen to the helpers.
If I need help, I can say, can you help me, please?
A helper will help me.
If I need a break, I can say, I need a break.
Asking for a break is a safe thing to do.
I can bring a small toy to hold.
I can hold [[GROWNUP]]'s hand.
I can squeeze [[GROWNUP]]'s hand three times.
Three squeezes mean I am here.
After the big day, I go home with [[GROWNUP]] and rest.
Sometimes new things feel scary.
Feeling scared is okay.
Many children feel scared about new things.
Feelings get smaller after some time.
I can breathe in slowly and breathe out slowly.
Then I can ask a helper for help.
If it is too loud or too bright, I can take a break.
I can count to ten.
I can hold [[GROWNUP]]'s hand.
A break can help me feel calm.
Then I can try again when I am ready.
At home, I can practise my big day with toys.
First, my toy gets ready.
Then my toy goes to the new place.
I can practise saying, can you help me, please?
Then my toy says, I need a break, and takes a break.
Here is my big day.
First, I get ready at home.
Then I go there with [[GROWNUP]].
Next, I do each part one step at a time.
After that, I go home.
I practised all the steps, and I did a good job.
